memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The angel added, "I will increase your descendants so much that they will be too numerous to count." - Gen 16:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Listen to the words God speaks to a runaway slave: "I will increase your descendants so much that they will be too numerous to count." This is remarkably similar to the promise God gave Abram himself (Gen 15:5). God lavishes on this Egyptian outsider a promise of blessing and multiplication that echoes His covenant with the patriarch.

What grace this reveals. Hagar was outside the covenant line - the child of promise would come through Sarah, not her. And yet God does not overlook her. He blesses her generously, giving her a future and a hope she could never have imagined. God's kindness spills far beyond the boundaries we might draw.

This tells us something wonderful about God's heart. He is not stingy with His goodness. Even those who seem to be on the margins of His plan are objects of His care. Hagar was not the chosen one, yet she was not forgotten. God had a blessing for her too.

There is comfort here for anyone who feels like an outsider - like the blessing is for others but not for them. God's compassion reaches to the edges. He blessed an Egyptian slave in the desert. In Christ, "there is neither Jew nor Gentile... for you are all one" (Gal 3:28), and God's blessing now flows freely to every people. You are never so far on the margins that God's kindness cannot reach you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you felt like an outsider to God's blessing?
- How does God's generosity to Hagar encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your kindness reaches even to the margins, even to the outsider. When I feel forgotten or on the edges, remind me that Your compassion has no boundaries. Thank You for blessing me in Christ.
Amen.
